root_cause: The shim advertises a single source-of-truth event envelope by re-exporting assistx.contracts when available and falling back to local mirrors otherwise, but the fallback implementation is incomplete and not guaranteed API-compatible with the canonical package, so consumers silently run against a divergent local implementation when the canonical package is unavailable.
plan: Document the advertised contract: canonical re-export with identical EventEnvelope, Actor, AuthState, EventLink, TraceEvent, TraceGroup and SCHEMA_VERSION, with fallback only for standalone runs.
Inspect the canonical assistx.contracts.event_envelope and assistx.contracts.version to capture exact public fields, types, defaults, ConfigDict and validators for all exported types.

Replace the stub class TraceEvent: pass and class TraceGroup: pass with full BaseModel mirrors matching the canonical definitions, and align Actor, EventLink and EventEnvelope fields, ConfigDict, defaults and validators to the canonical API.
Synchronize the fallback SCHEMA_VERSION and model definitions with the canonical source of truth and add a runtime compatibility assertion when canonical is importable to detect drift.

Add import-time tests that exercise the shim with canonical present and absent, asserting structural equivalence of the public API and that _USING_CANONICAL correctly reflects the import state while preserving standalone capability.
risks: Removing or altering the fallback breaks standalone runs that depend on local mirrors when assistx.contracts is not installed.
Hardcoded SCHEMA_VERSION in the fallback can drift from the canonical version, causing silent version skew in emitted envelopes.
Empty TraceEvent and TraceGroup stubs cause late runtime failures for consumers expecting real models, and the divergence is not observable at import time.
Consumers cannot detect they are using the fallback versus canonical without inspecting _USING_CANONICAL, leading to undetectable behavioral divergence.
